artifact.title: A soft dynamical central compensator is driven toward collapse unless its radial potential is parametrically stiff
artifact.status: exact conditional backreaction toy on the unrestricted desired-vacuum branch
artifact.question: If Q=q Q_0 is dynamical rather than fixed, does a conventional Lambda(q^2-1)^2 potential preserve enough repair strength?

setup.ray: Pure unrestricted repair with delta=kappa y, t=delta/4, y=q^2>=0.
setup.desiredBranch: Active squared amplitudes x_26=1/2-delta/8, x_29=3/10-11delta/80, x_5,10=1/5+delta/80, x_6,7=1/4-delta/16.

exact_elimination.direction: Throughout the viable delta window the numerator is positive, so finite-sector vacuum energy drives y_* below 1.

survival_condition.premise: For a bare kappa>24/61, require the backreacted delta_*=kappa y_* to remain at least 24/61.

examples.meaning: The near-threshold benchmark is extremely fragile.
Even the moderate benchmark needs a substantially stiff constraint.
The maximin-scale benchmark survives with a modestly stiff radial mode.

survival_condition.exact_constraint: A Lagrange-multiplier condition y=1 avoids the backreaction but makes Q kinematical rather than an ordinary soft field.

tuned_alternative.shiftedCenter: For Lambda(y-y0)^2, keeping y=1 stationary requires y0=1+kappa[(19/5)-(53/40)kappa]/(2Lambda).
tuned_alternative.interpretation: This is a calculable counter-shift but is a tuning unless derived from the same product geometry.

caveats: The eliminated energy formula is exact only while the desired active set remains the minimizing radial phase.

When delta falls below 24/61 the G direction condenses and a different branch must be minimized; the negative-y stationary examples should be read as collapse toward the y=0 boundary, not as physical negative q^2.
The toy treats one scalar amplitude q and omits angular/domain-wall fluctuations of a matrix-valued Q.
Loop corrections to Lambda and kappa are not included.
interpretation: Promoting Q to a soft order parameter is not automatically benign: the very repair term it creates gives matter an energetic incentive to reduce Q.
The robust kappa=20/19 region is dynamically preferable to the minimal kappa=2/5 point, not just Hessian-preferable.
This strengthens the case for either a constrained partial involution Q^3=Q or a genuinely heavy radial mode.
falsifiers: A full joint minimization including the G-condensed branches finds a stable y near one below the stated stiffness bound.
Additional product-action terms supply a positive y-linear contribution large enough to reverse the collapse force without tuning.
The physical trace prescription changes the sign of the matter energy derivative with respect to delta.
A matrix-valued constrained Q has light angular modes that destabilize the assumed one-amplitude reduction.

reproducibility.method: Exact rational elimination of the four active squared amplitudes.

next: Perform the full piecewise KKT minimization jointly in y, including the G-condensed branch.
Test whether the Spin(2,3) Cartan term supplies the required radial stiffness with the correct sign.
Construct the exact-constraint sigma-model version and count its angular modes.
artifact.conclusion: A soft Q is viable only with a meaningful stiffness hierarchy. Near the repair threshold the required hierarchy diverges; the kappa=20/19 maximin region is much more tolerant, while an exact partial-involution constraint removes radial collapse by construction.

artifact.title: The finite compensator trace normalization is rigid across all 44 robust carriers
artifact.question: Does coupling the Spin(2,3) compensator to the central partial involution introduce carrier-dependent gravitational normalization?

definitions.node_charge: q(i)=+1 on A, -1 on B, and 0 otherwise.
definitions.left_right: Q_L acts by q(i) on a positive module (i,j) and by q(j) on its J-swapped partner; Q_R acts oppositely.
definitions.sample: All 44 robust 184-dimensional carriers with trace split (k5,k10)=(8,4).

exact_census.preferredCarrier: The preferred carrier has exactly the same tuple (184,0,88,-16,16).

one_sided.limitation: A single side generates only the corresponding commutator norm and does not reproduce the full left-plus-right repair.

side_doubled.compensator: On an auxiliary two-state side label, Q_side=diag(Q_L,Q_R) and C=N tensor Q_side.
side_doubled.repair: The finite commutator norm is exactly the sum of left and right unrestricted commutator norms, up to the already explicit factor 1/4 in U(D).
side_doubled.implication: A minimal side doublet implements the full v519 unrestricted ray without choosing left over right.

combined_without_doubling.warning: Q_L+/-Q_R is not generally a partial involution and changes the field weights, so these are not equivalent replacements.

interpretation: The product construction's Cartan-sector multiplicity is invariant over the entire robust carrier family.
Graph variation inside the 44-carrier class therefore cannot tune the ratio between the spacetime compensator term and the finite repair term.
The vanishing signed trace means A and B support is dimension-balanced even though their overlap has negative correlation Tr(Q_L Q_R)=-16.
Any phenomenologically required rescaling must come from trace normalization, the product coupling, or additional representation multiplicity rather than carrier selection.
falsifiers: A robust carrier omitted from the enumeration has a different trace tuple.
The exact quotient representation changes module multiplicities or the J-swapped completion.
The physically admissible product trace is weighted rather than the ordinary finite trace and breaks the census invariance.
The auxiliary side doublet is forbidden by grading, real-structure, or KO-sign constraints.

reproducibility.method: Exact integer sums of dim(i)dim(j) over positive modules and their J-swapped partners.

next: Insert the side doublet into the explicit KO6 real structure and test signs.
Derive the relative Cartan/finite coefficient after fixing normalized versus unnormalized traces.
Promote Q to a constrained field and quantify radial backreaction.
artifact.conclusion: The robust family has a universal finite compensator normalization: Tr(Q_L^2)=Tr(Q_R^2)=88. A two-state side lift gives the full left-plus-right repair with trace factor 176, but removes carrier choice as a way to tune its gravitational feedback.

artifact.title: Explicit Cl(2,3) matrices eliminate the product-compensator mixed term

conventions.representation: 4x4 complex irreducible Clifford matrices built from Pauli Kronecker products

exactChecks.brokenDerivative: [J_a4,N]=plus or minus Gamma_a for every a

consequence.split: For the ordinary Hilbert-Schmidt trace, ||[D,C]||^2 separates into a Cartan/coframe term and a finite [D_F,Q] term with no bilinear cross operator.
consequence.reason: The finite-direction spin factor gamma_*N is scalar while each broken Cartan derivative is a traceless gamma matrix.
consequence.robustness: The cancellation follows from Clifford parity/tracelessness, not a numerical accident of matrix entries.

qualification: The calculation uses the ordinary positive Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint. The Lorentzian/Krein action may insert a fundamental symmetry and must be checked separately.
Connection, form-degree, and spacetime index contractions were suppressed; they can change signs though not the bare spin trace.
The result validates mixed-term cancellation, not the normalization of kappa_U.
falsifiers: The programme's admitted Krein adjoint turns the zero ordinary trace into a nonzero physical mixed term.
The exact product Dirac operator uses a chirality/compensator placement for which gamma_*N is not scalar.
Form-degree contractions introduce an independent mixed invariant despite the spin trace.
Reality doubling changes the cancellation or the relative sign of the two squared pieces.
next: Repeat the trace using the exact Hilbert-to-Krein fundamental symmetry already developed in the programme.
Carry differential-form and connection indices through the product reduction.
Compute Tr_F(Q^2) and the finite commutator coefficient in the 184-dimensional carrier.
Check whether both reduced terms have positive physical signs after Lorentzian continuation.
artifact.conclusion: In a concrete minimal Cl(2,3) representation, the product-compensator cross term vanishes identically and the Cartan and finite commutator energies decouple at quadratic order. The next obstruction is signature/Krein sign, not Clifford mixing.

The one-Beta trace is not a substitute action here because it annihilates both desired pure terms.
